repairs.text: Strongest feature: Aron Ra challenges Hernandez’s inference from indivisible person-status to an indivisible substance by observing that personhood is not measured as bodily height or weight, so a categorical status need not divide with physical quantities. Principal limitation: His compressed wording treats the target too narrowly and offers no physical account of unified agency, persistence, component replacement, or subjective identity, leaving Hernandez’s broader concern only partly answered. Live burden: Aron Ra must explain how an organized material system instantiates complete personhood without portions becoming fractional persons, and identify what continuity of organization preserves one subject through bodily turnover. Locked score: The locked score of 77 reflects a conceptual objection that weakens the affirmative inference, while its thin warrant, unclear phrasing, and incomplete treatment of persistence prevent greater force.

Strongest feature: Aron Ra offers two checks on the inference from out-of-body experiences to bodily departure: peer-reviewed findings conflict, and brain stimulation through the god helmet reportedly reproduces the effects. Principal limitation: He provides no studies, methods, controls, effect frequencies, or comparisons of evidential quality, while saying the helmet duplicates all effects exceeds the unspecific detail offered and obscures differences among experiences. Live burden: Aron Ra must specify which sensations or observations were reproduced, establish how closely they match the reports at issue, and explain how the competing research should reduce confidence without claiming to disprove every experience. Locked score: The locked score of 73 recognizes empirical counterevidence against the paranormal interpretation, but limited sourcing, precision, and calibration keep the objection from carrying stronger evidential weight.
